rows.title: Skew Bilinear Cancellation of the Trace and Quadratic Terms

maturity_record.invariant: A skew-symmetric matrix contracted against a symmetric matrix has zero trace, and a skew-symmetric matrix annihilates its own quadratic form: the two algebraic cancellations behind the manuscript's solenoidal expansion, holding unconditionally on the stated symmetry hypotheses.
maturity_record.assumption_review: Plain finite real matrices indexed by Fin n with explicit pointwise symmetry hypotheses; no continuum Hessian, no smoothness structure, and no numerical witness is claimed.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: Both cancellations are exact identities on their hypothesis classes, witnessed by any nonzero skew matrix against a nonzero symmetric one.

rows.title: The Three-Term Solenoidal Expansion and Its Conditional Drop

maturity_record.invariant: The weighted divergence of the candidate current decomposes exactly into the trace slot, the transport-divergence slot, and the density coupling slot; under the stationary coupling the identity reads tr(Q H) - g^T Q g + (div Q)^T g; both cancellable terms die on the skew and symmetric hypotheses, and the remaining drop holds only under an explicit extra hypothesis (orthogonality or spatially constant Q), with a concrete remainder datum where it does not.
maturity_record.assumption_review: Directional derivative data is explicit (H for the Hessian slot, DQ for the transport-divergence slot); the coupling is an explicit hypothesis, not a solved PDE; the weighted divergence is defined by the exact Leibniz decomposition rather than a discretization of Fokker-Planck.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: The remainder witness evaluates to exactly 1 on concrete two-direction derivative data, so the unconditional drop is not vacuously unreachable.

theorem fep163_solenoidal_expansion {n : ℕ} (Q H DQ : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ)
    (g dlogp : Fin n → ℝ) (hcoup : ∀ i, dlogp i = -g i) :
    weightedDivergence Q H DQ g dlogp
      = traceOf (mulOf Q H) - dot g (mulVec Q g) + dot (divQ DQ) g

theorem fep163_weightedDivergence_eq {n : ℕ} (Q H DQ : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ)
    (g dlogp : Fin n → ℝ) :
    weightedDivergence Q H DQ g dlogp
      = traceOf (mulOf Q H) + dot (divQ DQ) g + dot (mulVec Q g) dlogp

rows.title: Graph Divergence of the Candidate Solenoidal Current

maturity_record.invariant: On a finite node set the node divergence of the skew transport field is twice its row sum; the node divergence of the edge current splits into the transport slot plus the discrete-divergence slot; and the weighted node divergence obeys an exact Leibniz rule whose p-residual does not vanish by skewness alone.
maturity_record.assumption_review: Edge fields are plain real matrices with the flux convention W i j = flux i to j; the weighted statements assume a strictly positive density; no continuum graph limit or first-order asymptotic identification is claimed.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: The decomposition and the Leibniz rule are exact on every finite node set, and the residual term is generically nonzero by nodeDiv_skew.

theorem fep164_graphDecomposition {n : ℕ} (Q : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ)
    (g : Fin n → ℝ) (hQ : SkewSymmetric Q) (i : Fin n) :
    nodeDiv (currentOf Q g) i = mulVec Q g i + g i * rowSum Q i
qualified_declaration_statements.fep164_nodeDiv_skew:
theorem fep164_nodeDiv_skew {n : ℕ} {Q : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ} (hQ : SkewSymmetric Q)
    (i : Fin n) : nodeDiv Q i = 2 * rowSum Q i
qualified_declaration_statements.fep164_weightedNodeDiv_eq:
theorem fep164_weightedNodeDiv_eq {n : ℕ} (W : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ)
    {p : Fin n → ℝ} (hp : ∀ i, 0 < p i) (i : Fin n) :
    weightedNodeDiv p W i =
      nodeDiv W i + ∑ j, (1 - p j / p i) * W j i
qualified_declaration_statements.fep164_weightedCurrent_div_eq:
theorem fep164_weightedCurrent_div_eq {n : ℕ} (Q : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ)
    (g : Fin n → ℝ) {p : Fin n → ℝ} (hQ : SkewSymmetric Q)
    (hp : ∀ i, 0 < p i) (i : Fin n) :
    weightedNodeDiv p (currentOf Q g) i
      = mulVec Q g i + g i * rowSum Q i
        + g i * ∑ j, (1 - p j / p i) * Q j i

rows.statement_review: On directed edge matrices with outflow-minus-inflow node divergence, skew Q gives nodeDiv Q=2rowSum Q. For currentOf(Q,g)(i,j)=Qij*g_j its node divergence is Qg_i+g_i*rowSum_i. Positive node weights yield an exact additional weighted residual.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: This is graph algebra, not an analytic divergence discretization theorem. Positive density need not normalize; currentOf is an edge field whereas mulVec Qg is a node vector. Residual can vanish on special data and is not forced nonzero solely by nodeDiv_skew.

rows.adverse_witness_specification_unexecuted: A balanced skew cycle may have rowSum0, so skewness does not force a nonzero row sum. Constant g or special densities can cancel terms; no universal residual sign follows.

rows.title: Frobenius Least-Squares Projection of the Symmetrizer

maturity_record.invariant: For symmetric S the squared Frobenius norm splits exactly as ||H - S||^2 = ||H - symmetrize H||^2 + ||symmetrize H - S||^2, the symmetrizer minimizes the squared distance among symmetric matrices with equality exactly at the symmetrizer, the symmetric minimizer is unique, and the concrete nonsymmetric datum [[0,1],[0,0]] carries residual exactly 1/2.
maturity_record.assumption_review: Matrix projection only, no differentiability, no continuum Clairaut theorem, no Bregman-projection existence/uniqueness claim.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: The residual example evaluates to exactly 1/2 on nonsymmetric data, and symmetric data attains the zero residual exactly at the symmetrizer, so both the strict and the degenerate boundary are realized.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep167_frobenius_pythagoras:
theorem fep167_frobenius_pythagoras {n : ℕ} (H S : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ)
    (hS : SymmetricOf S) :
    frobeniusSq (H - S)
      = frobeniusSq (H - symmetrize H) + frobeniusSq (symmetrize H - S)
qualified_declaration_statements.fep167_symmetrize_minimizes:
theorem fep167_symmetrize_minimizes {n : ℕ} (H S : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ)
    (hS : SymmetricOf S) :
    frobeniusSq (H - symmetrize H) ≤ frobeniusSq (H - S)
      ∧ (frobeniusSq (H - symmetrize H) = frobeniusSq (H - S) ↔ S = symmetrize H)
qualified_declaration_statements.fep167_projection_unique:
theorem fep167_projection_unique {n : ℕ} (H S : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ)
    (hS : SymmetricOf S)
    (hmin : ∀ T : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ, SymmetricOf T →
      frobeniusSq (H - S) ≤ frobeniusSq (H - T)) :
    S = symmetrize H

theorem fep167_residual_example :
    frobeniusSq (fep167ResidualH - symmetrize fep167ResidualH) = 1 / 2
      ∧ frobeniusSq (fep167ResidualH - symmetrize fep167ResidualH) ≠ 0
